title: Priority Hub Week compact and ask curation
content:
Purpose:
- Create a concise, repeatable week-long alignment ("Priority Hub Week") for the company to accelerate decisioning on top cross-functional bets.
- Deliver an all-staff update and a short runway of OKRs to inform team roadmaps and resourcing asks.

Audience:
- Execs, ELT, all engineering and product leads, growth & support leads, and ops partners.

High-level outcomes we want by end of Priority Hub Week (T+5):
1) Finalize top 3 company OKRs for the upcoming quarter with committed owners.
2) Publish an all-staff run-of-show + exec update slide pack for the company meeting.
3) Identify 2 cross-team blockers to unblock immediately (resourcing, infra, compliance).
4) Produce a short decision ledger (who decided, what, and rollback criteria).

Proposed cadence and format (working draft):
Day 0 (prep): ask teams to submit 1-page signals: metric delta, risk, ask (one-line). Deadline EOD Day 0.
Day 1: Leadership alignment (ELT) deep-dive, narrow candidate OKRs. 90 min.
Day 2: Cross-functional triage workshops (two parallel rooms):
  - Room A: Product + Eng (hosting, dedicated, private gap analysis)
  - Room B: GTM + CS + Ops (pricing, SLAs, customer asks)
  Outcome: top candidate OKRs + 1–2 known blockers per OKR.
Day 3: Resource & rollout planning: draft staffing, infra capacity, and canary/rollback plans.
Day 4: Exec decision session: commit final OKRs and owners. 60 min.
Day 5: Publish all-staff brief + run-of-show for town hall; prepare Q&A and exec talking points.

Draft candidate company OKRs (ranked):
- OKR A: Reduce per-token serving cost by 18% while maintaining quality SLA:
  - KR1: Deploy two prioritized quantization profiles to 3 high-volume models (by month 2).
  - KR2: Implement prefix/KV cache for 4 highest-traffic endpoints (observed token savings >=12%).
  - KR3: Lower queue-time P95 by 20ms via routing and batching improvements.
  Owner: VP Serving Runtime (tentative).

- OKR B: Improve outage resilience and graceful degradation across Hosted + Dedicated + Private:
  - KR1: Add automated fallback for top 5 models across regions (tested in staging).
  - KR2: Reduce incident MTTR for inference errors by 30% with runbooks and synthetic monitors.
  - KR3: Complete Private deployment audit checklist for SOC readiness for two pilot customers.
  Owner: VP SRE.

- OKR C: Speed up developer onboarding to inference features (increase PLG funnel efficiency):
  - KR1: Reduce median time-to-first-call from signup to first inference by 40%.
  - KR2: Publish 6 turnkey quickstarts + 3 reference architectures for common integration patterns.
  - KR3: Launch an in-console cost-optimizer recommendation panel for top 50 beta users.
  Owner: VP Developer Experience.

Notes-to-self / drafting fragments (informal):
- Need metric baselines for KR targets (Maya to pull usage heatmap by 02/12).
- Is 18% cost reduction aggressive? Might re-frame as "18% target with 95% confidence interval".
- Consider a safety net budget for Dedicated capacity during the rollout window.

All-staff run-of-show (20–30 min town hall + 20 min open Q&A):
- 00:00–00:03 Opening (CEO) — 3 slides: northstar recap, why Priority Hub Week matters.
- 00:03–00:10 Executives roundup (product + infra + biz ops) — 3 minute updates each.
- 00:10–00:18 Finalized OKRs & owners (PM 1) — 2 slides per OKR: what success looks like, key risks.
- 00:18–00:23 Quick wins & immediate asks — 5 quick bullet items with owners.
- 00:23–00:30 Live Q&A (moderated) — topics triaged ahead of time + live questions.

Draft exec talking points (short):
- Anchor: Our northstar is predictable, economical inference for builders. These OKRs are tactical steps to keep that promise.
- Emphasize tradeoffs: cost vs latency vs quality; we will instrument regressions and require signoff for model-level changes.
- Reassure: we will maintain fallbacks in early rollouts to minimize customer impact.

Risk register (top 6 quick list):
- Risk 1: Quality regression from quantization. Mitigation: hold regression evals + canary on 10% traffic.
- Risk 2: Capacity shortfall during Dedicated burst window. Mitigation: reserve burst buffer + cross-region failover.
- Risk 3: Conflicting resource priorities across Eng orgs. Mitigation: ELT arbitration + temporary IC reassignments.
- Risk 4: Compliance gating for Private pilots. Mitigation: parallel audit tracks and one-off expert scrum.
- Risk 5: Poor customer communication during changes. Mitigation: CS-run playbook and early beta outreach.
- Risk 6: Town hall noise — unresolved asks increasing anxiety. Mitigation: publish follow-up timeline and decision ledger within 24h.

Decisions needed from ELT before Day 1:
- Approve Priority Hub Week calendar and 4-hour blocking reserve for leads.
- Endorse the three candidate OKRs as the starting slate.
- Commit a small contingency budget (up to $75k) for Dedicated burst and audit compliance support.

Open questions for follow-up: 
- Who owns the decision ledger (write/read permissions)? (Ops suggested answer: company-ops will maintain.)
- What is the exact measurement framework for "per-token serving cost" — dollar per 1k tokens or normalized cost model?
- Should Private audit work be a separate objective or a sub-KR under resilience?

Immediate asks (action items):
- Maya Chen: export usage heatmap + top endpoints by token volume (due 02/12).
- Priya Singh: draft the all-staff slide deck skeleton (due 02/13).
- Ethan Morales: prepare staging playbook for canaries and fallback tests (due 02/14).
- Riley Patel: lock calendar, send invites, and create ELT pre-read doc (due 02/11).

Appendix (short):
- Quick references: current monthly token spend baseline: $1.2M (Feb 2026), P95 latency per-host: 210ms (hosted), Dedicated pooled utilization: 68%.
- Suggested pre-read links: see linked_artifacts.

Voice notes and shorthand (raw):
- "If we can show 10–12% token savings from prefix caching in 2 weeks that's a win — rest is optimization."
- "Town hall: 20 min crisp + 20 Q&A; moderator to triage Slack thread in advance."
- "Follow-up: publish decision ledger + short 'what we tried' after 1 month."

-- end of working draft --
